correctness.rationale: For composite m, if p is the least prime factor, \(c(m)=m-\varphi(m)\ge m/p\ge\sqrt m\), so \(F(m)<m\) for composites \(m\ge26\). For primes \(p\ge29\), \(F(p)=p+2\); if p+2 is composite, \(F^2(p)=p+5-c(p+2)<p\), and if p+2 is prime then p+4 is divisible by 3 and \(F^3(p)\le2(p+4)/3+3<p\). Hence every \(n\ge26\) has a smaller iterate within three steps. Strong induction forces eventual entry into the invariant interval 1..25. The fully displayed exact 25-state transition graph has precisely the cycles (9), (11,13,15), (23,25). The two-cycle establishes sharpness at 25. Every globally attracting invariant set contains all three cycles, and their union itself attracts every orbit. The included script independently cross-checks totients by factorization and sieve, all 25 states, and one million initial values; only the symbolic inequalities yield the infinite claim. The argument has no unproved conditional premise.

value.rationale: Complete periodic spectra and sharp globally absorbing sets are canonical qualitative and quantitative invariants of nonmonotone arithmetic dynamical systems. This result changes the status of the k=3 shifted Euler map from eventual periodicity (for each start, as previously proved) to a universal exact classification: precisely three cycles of lengths 1, 2, and 3, six periodic points, and an optimal start-independent finite trap. The sharpness and all-start quantifier make it a structural natural classification rather than an arbitrary finite experiment; it also establishes strong uniform information not supplied by a T-dependent bound.
